title: Introduce pluggable serializer + shard reconciler for heterogenous weight artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: our model ingestion path currently needs bespoke ad-hoc logic for several weight packaging variants and a separate tokenizer bootstrap path that assumes a single canonical manifest. This increases surface area for bugs, slows onboarding of new model formats, and forces runtime branching that degrades warm-start latency.

Goal: create a small, well-documented pluggable serializer interface (Serializer v1) and a runtime Shard Reconciler layer that can normalize divergent weight manifests and shard tiling into a consistent in-memory activation stream. Also introduce a Tokenizer Placement abstraction that makes tokenizer initialization idempotent and retry-safe across lazy activation.

Scope: implement Serializer v1 adapters for the 3 dominant formats we ingest (legacy tarball, indexed bundle, cloud-sliced shards), a Reconciler that runs before activation to produce an ordered load plan, and a thin Tokenizer Placement shim. Provide migration tooling to generate reconciler hints for historically ingested models.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change on-disk checkpoint formats across customers or implement a new universal on-disk format. Quantization code paths are out of scope except where needed to read metadata for reconciliation.

Constraints: keep public runtime contracts unchanged (API surface and model manifest URI). Target no regression in 99th percentile cold-start latency > 5% and aim to reduce average cold-start by at least 15% for common shard distributions.
acceptance_criteria: Serializer v1 interface added and documented in codebase (public API doc link included in related_docs)
Adapters implemented for legacy-tar, indexed-bundle, cloud-shard and covered by unit tests
Shard Reconciler produces an ordered activation plan that passes 4 synthetic model families in the compatibility matrix
End-to-end ingestion benchmark: average cold-start time reduced at least 15% for sample workload; 99th percentile regression <5%
Tokenizer Placement shim ensures tokenizer init is idempotent and retry-safe when loader reorders shards
Migration tool generates reconciliation hints for >= 95% of historical models in s3://redwood-models/legacy/ and has a dry-run mode
Code reviewed by Runtime and Platform leads and merged behind feature flag; rollout plan added to PR description
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed. Validated approach to insert a reconciler that canonicalizes 'tile' vs 'shard' nomenclature. Prototype reduces branching in loader by centralizing decisions.

2026-03-04: Design review with Runtime (Marcus, Elena) and PM (Sara). Decision: keep existing manifest URI contract; reconciler emits a transient activation plan rather than rewriting stored manifests.
2026-03-06: First adapter (indexed-bundle) implemented + unit tests. Benchmarks show a 12% cold-start improvement for that family in local perf harness.
2026-03-08: PR feedback from Security: ensure serializer adapter validates manifest signatures and rejects malformed shard ranges. Added validation task and opened follow-up ENG-74389.

2026-03-09: Integration test flake observed when tokenizer re-init races with deferred activation; added a Tokenizer Placement shim to sequence initialization. Discussed retry semantics with Design; approved.

2026-03-10: Performance run against canary fleet scheduled for 2026-03-12. Rollout will be behind feature flag 'loader.reconciler_v1' with gradual traffic ramp and automatic rollback on latency regression >5%.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: rewriting on-disk manifests was simpler for downstream consumers but deemed too risky for migration; we instead chose a transient activation plan to preserve backwards compatibility.

Follow-ups: attach a post-rollout validation job to compare activation-order histograms with historical baseline; open a separate ticket to cover quantized format adapters if customers request (suggested ENG-74400).
